title: New NIR-emissive tetranuclear Er(III) complexes with 4-hydroxo-2,1,3-benzothiadiazolate and dibenzoylmethanide ligands: synthesis and characterization

synthesis.procedure: Modified one-step procedure: at ambient temperature, KOtBu (0.151 g, 1.34 mmol) and Hdbm (0.204 g, 0.910 mmol) were dissolved in methanol (7 mL). A solution of ErCl3·6H2O (0.177 g, 0.464 mmol) in methanol (5 mL) was added, giving an immediate yellowish precipitate. The mixture was stirred overnight, the solvent was removed under reduced pressure, and the residue was treated with methylene chloride (10 mL). The suspension was centrifuged, hexane (15 mL) was added to the solution, and the precipitate was collected and dried. An additional crop was obtained by evaporating the mother liquor to ~5 mL.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-step precipitation; centrifugation of CH2Cl2 suspension
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Solvent distilled off under reduced pressure; residue treated with CH2Cl2 (10 mL), centrifuged, hexane (15 mL) added; precipitate collected and dried; additional crop from mother liquor evaporated to ~5 mL.

properties.summary: Used as a comparison compound: (dbm)−-centered absorption at 350 nm sensitizes Er(III) NIR emission (4I13/2 → 4I15/2) in prior work, but under the identical dilute CH2Cl2 conditions used here the NIR intensity was practically at the noise level versus 1 and 2.

measurements.name: NIR emission intensity vs 1 and 2
measurements.conditions: 0.1 mM in CH2Cl2; λexc = 350 nm; same instrument conditions as 1 and 2

source_locations.location: Spectral properties of the complexes; Fig. 3

synthesis.procedure: Two approaches. Preferred ligand-substitution route (b): [Er5(dbm)10(OH)5] (0.082 g, 0.026 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL) was treated with OH-btd (0.020 g, 0.13 mmol, 5 equiv.) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL); after 2 days an orange precipitate of 1 was collected, washed with CH2Cl2 and dried in vacuo (0.060 g, 70%). Alternative (a): Hdbm (0.075 g, 0.34 mmol) and OH-btd (0.051 g, 0.34 mmol) in MeOH (5 mL) with NEt3 (0.18 mL), then ErCl3·6H2O (0.128 g, 0.335 mmol) in MeOH (5 mL); after 1 day the orange solid was extracted with toluene and dried to give 1 (0.026 g, 10%). Route (c) gave 1 by drying 1·3.5CH2Cl2 (80% based on OH-btd).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: ligand substitution in CH2Cl2 or one-pot MeOH/NEt3 precipitation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange precipitate washed with CH2Cl2 (or MeOH) and dried in vacuo; recrystallization from toluene gives 1·7C7H8, which dries to solvent-free 1.
synthesis.yield: 0.060 g (70%) by route b; 0.026 g (10%) by route a

properties.summary: μeff at 300 K matches four non-interacting Er(III) 4I15/2 ions (g = 6/5); Curie–Weiss behavior with a small negative θ suggests weak antiferromagnetic interactions or ligand-field depopulation of mJ sublevels. Excitation at 450 nm (O-btd-centered) gives Er(III) NIR luminescence at ~1530 nm; 360 nm excitation gives only ligand fluorescence at 510 nm. NIR intensity is lower than for 2, consistent with fewer (O-btd)− antenna ligands.

measurements.name: electronic absorption maximum
measurements.conditions: 0.01 mM in CH2Cl2; shoulders at 310–330 and 430–450 nm

measurements.name: ligand-centered emission
measurements.conditions: λexc = 360 nm; 0.01 mM CH2Cl2; slit 14 nm

measurements.name: Er(III) NIR emission
measurements.conditions: λexc = 450 nm; 0.1 mM CH2Cl2; aerated; ambient temperature

synthesis.procedure: Obtained by extraction of the crude one-pot MeOH/NEt3 product of ErCl3·6H2O, Hdbm and OH-btd with toluene (25 mL) followed by slow evaporation at room temperature, or by recrystallization of solvent-free 1 from toluene. Drying in vacuo affords 1.
synthesis.time: reaction mixture stirred 1 day; then slow evaporation of toluene extract
synthesis.vessel_or_method: extraction into toluene and slow evaporation; alternatively recrystallization of 1 from toluene
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals of 1·7C7H8; vacuum drying yields solvent-free 1.
synthesis.yield: 0.026 g (10%) of 1 after drying the toluene solvate (route a)

properties.summary: Magnetism and luminescence were reported for solvent-free 1, not specifically for the toluene solvate crystals.

source_locations.location: Preparation of 1 and solvates; Experimental route a

synthesis.procedure: [Er5(dbm)10(OH)5] (0.058 g, 0.018 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (5 mL) was treated with OH-btd (0.0028 g, 0.018 mmol), stirred for 4 days, and n-hexane (10 mL) was layered on the solution. After solvent diffusion at ambient temperature, orange crystals of 1·3.5CH2Cl2 (slightly contaminated with unreacted starting cluster) were obtained; washing with a small amount of CH2Cl2 gave the pure solvate. Vacuum drying afforded 1 (0.010 g, 80% based on OH-btd).
synthesis.time: stirred 4 days, then layered diffusion until mixing ceased
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals washed with a little CH2Cl2; vacuum drying gives 1.
synthesis.yield: 0.010 g of 1 after drying (80% on OH-btd)

properties.summary: Characterized by single-crystal XRD; magnetic and optical data refer to desolvated 1.

synthesis.procedure: Highest-yield one-pot route (b): Hdbm (0.074 g, 0.33 mmol) and OH-btd (0.075 g, 0.49 mmol) in methanol (7 mL) with triethylamine (0.24 mL) were stirred 1 h at ambient temperature; ErCl3·6H2O (0.126 g, 0.329 mmol) in methanol (5 mL) was added, giving an immediate orange precipitate. After stirring overnight, 2 was collected, washed with methanol and dried (0.193 g, 95%). Route (c): [Er5(dbm)10(OH)5] (0.041 g, 0.013 mmol) with OH-btd (0.020 g, 0.13 mmol) in CH2Cl2 gave 2 after 1 day (0.028 g, 70%). Route (a) via THF recrystallization of a CH2Cl2 substitution product gave 2 after drying 2·6THF (~5%).
synthesis.time: 1 h ligand deprotonation then overnight after metal addition (route b); 1 day (route c)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-pot MeOH/NEt3 precipitation or CH2Cl2 ligand substitution
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange precipitate washed with methanol or CH2Cl2 and dried in vacuo; recrystallization from THF gives 2·6THF.
synthesis.yield: 0.193 g (95%) route b; 0.028 g (70%) route c; ~5% via 2·6THF (route a)

properties.summary: μeff at 300 K matches four non-interacting Er(III) ions; Curie–Weiss θ is slightly negative. Stronger Er(III) NIR emission at ~1530 nm (λexc = 450 nm) than complex 1, attributed to the higher (O-btd)− : (dbm)− ratio. Ligand fluorescence at 510 nm is observed upon 360 nm excitation. Accurate lifetime data were not obtained because of low solubility.

measurements.name: electronic absorption maximum
measurements.conditions: 0.01 mM in CH2Cl2; shoulders at 310–330 and 430–450 nm

measurements.name: Er(III) NIR emission
measurements.conditions: λexc = 450 nm; 0.1 mM CH2Cl2; aerated; ambient temperature; intensity higher than 1

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear {Er4(OH)2} heteroleptic dbm/O-btd THF solvate; packing chains via short S···N contacts

synthesis.procedure: OH-btd (0.040 g, 0.26 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL) was added to [Er5(dbm)10(OH)5] (0.188 g, 0.0588 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL). After 2 days the orange precipitate was washed, dried, and dissolved in hot THF (10 mL). Slow evaporation at ambient temperature gave orange crystals of 2·6THF. Recrystallization of independently prepared 2 from THF also yields 2·6THF. Vacuum drying removes all THF to give 2.
synthesis.temperature: ambient temperature; hot THF for dissolution
synthesis.time: 2 days precipitation, then slow evaporation of THF
synthesis.vessel_or_method: ligand substitution then recrystallization from hot THF by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals of 2·6THF; vacuum drying yields 2.
synthesis.yield: ~5% of desolvated 2 from this THF route

properties.summary: Single-crystal XRD structure; magnetic and luminescence measurements were performed on desolvated 2.
